name: Wastage log from a bin photo
summary: Turns a bin photo into a wastage entry on the stock record: matches the photo to a catalogue item, queues the adjustment to waste for approval, and writes a daily waste summary. Crons read and draft; a person approves every stock change.

covered_by.waste-trigger: skill (a person logs the waste; no platform trigger is mapped)
covered_by.bin-photo: skill (the agent reads the photo; no photo intake is mapped)
covered_by.cost-value: gap (Square's COGS report is in the dashboard; no API operation mapped)
covered_by.menu-action: gap (86 availability not mapped to an operation here)
covered_by.record-keeping: draft (daily summary record in the workflow store)

crons.name: catalogue
crons.summary: Hourly: read the catalogue items that photos are matched against, and the adjustment reasons available.

crons.name: log-waste
crons.summary: Check each identified waste entry, then queue its adjustment to waste for approval. Parks any entry that does not check out.

crons.name: review
crons.summary: Daily (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia): summarise the last day's waste adjustments into the store.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations only read Square and write a summary into the workflow store. The one stock change, the adjustment to WASTE, is a live operation: a cron can only queue it and a person approves it.

square.covers: catalogue read, adjustment reasons, the day's waste changes, and the waste adjustment queued for approval

gaps: Eats365 and Lightspeed: help pages were read, but neither has a platform in the kit, so no adapter, operations or tests exist. Waste logging for those POS systems needs their APIs mapped first.
Photo intake: no mapped platform receives bin photos. The agent reads a photo handed to it, and a person or the CRM shell writes the waste entry into the store.
The waste trigger, the reason picked at the POS, and waste photos are not covered in the pages read. A live Square account is needed to confirm whether the POS asks for a reason on a waste entry.

Three read operations are POST-shaped and marked write in the kit (search, batch retrieve). On a deploy where KIT_ALLOW_WRITES is 0 they are refused. Their read-only status is not changed here because core/ is not edited.
COGS and profit margin: Square's COGS report is in the dashboard only, so cost-value is not automated.
Purchase orders, staff feedback and 86 availability are not automated.
The Square adapter is docs-only until a Square sandbox account proves it. The offline test uses a fake network only.

evidence.calls: 3 calls read in the variants file; none described how waste is logged, so the steps come from the platform pages. The worklist counts 1 call.
evidence.platforms: 3 platforms with pages read (Eats365, Lightspeed, Square). Only Square has a kit platform, with mapped inventory operations for catalogue, adjustment reasons, changes and adjustments to WASTE.
